study: A simulated hand trained to play held-back phrases and chords at four keys
what: A muscle-control policy for a simulated four-key hand, trained on requested phrases and scored on phrase orders, rhythms, chords, tempos and starting poses set aside before tuning. No brain recording drove it.

numbers.what: key strikes the final policy made as intended, over all held-back phrases (every strike asked for)
two-key chords the final policy played correctly (every chord asked for)

printed_without_macro.what: held-back phrases the final policy played without a fault
held-back phrases (eight phrase orders, two tempos, two starting poses)
held-back phrases played without a fault by the starting policy
held-back phrases played without a fault by the first new fit
held-back phrases played without a fault by the reference controller
held-back phrases played with no muscle command
saved example phrase: strikes made as intended (of the same number asked for)
saved example phrase: chords played correctly (of the same number asked for)
saved example phrase: largest timing error, seconds (printed as 34 ms)

why_some_numbers_have_no_macro: Whole numbers below 100, and round numbers that double as percentages or durations elsewhere in the papers, have no macro: the build would otherwise refuse the same digits wherever another section types them as an ordinary number. The papers print them as words or as plain digits; each is listed here with its source so that it can be checked.
limits: A simulation: a generic hand with wrist, thumb and finger spreading braced, following scripted fingertip paths. No living hand learned anything.
The held-back phrases are eight orders at two tempos from two starting poses, not independent subjects.
The first scoring program was terminated (exit code 143) after it had saved its complete results; why is unknown. A separate full replay finished cleanly and agreed.
The simulated keys have soft limits, so key travel can pass the nominal 6 mm.
credit: Hand model: MyoSim; simulator: MuJoCo; environment: MyoSuite.
